#  {.sidebar}

**Student Social Media Addiction Analysis** is built from survey-based data on social media usage habits and addiction levels among students. Each row represents one student's response.

---

**Coverage:** 110+ countries · High school, undergraduate & graduate levels

**Variables:** Age, gender, relationship status, sleep hours, most-used platform, daily usage hours, academic performance effects, and mental health & addiction scores.

---

*Dataset by Zahra Nusrat — collected to understand the extent of social media dependency among students and to identify patterns that may contribute to unhealthy usage behavior.*

---

**Additional Resources For Further Investigation**

- [Nature: Social Media & Sleep Study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-35779-w)
- [Springer: Community Health Impact](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10900-026-01578-7)


---

```{r}
# Reading in the data 
social <- read_csv(here("Students Social Media Addiction.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Takes one obs per student ID
social <- social |>
  group_by(Student_ID) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup()
```

### Column {width="50%"}

```{r}
#| title: Amount of Students per Age Group

# Making a line graph of the total amount of students per age group
social |>
  count(Age) |>
  ggplot(aes(Age, n)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5, color = "#4A78A6") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#6AA6A6") +
  labs(x = "Age Group", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

```

### Column {width="50%"}

```{r}
#| title: Average Sleep and Daily Usage by Mental Health Score

# Average Sleep and Daily Usage by Mental Health Score 
useage_summary = social |>
  mutate(MH_cate = case_when(
    Mental_Health_Score < 5 ~ "Low (0-4)", 
    Mental_Health_Score < 8 ~ "Moderate (5-7)", 
    Mental_Health_Score <= 10 ~ "High (8-10)"), 
    MH_cate = factor(MH_cate,
                     levels = c("Low (0-4)", 
                                           "Moderate (5-7)", 
                                           "High (8-10)"))) |>
  group_by(MH_cate) |>
  summarise(
    avg_sleep = mean(Sleep_Hours_Per_Night, na.rm = TRUE), 
    avg_usage = mean(Avg_Daily_Usage_Hours, na.rm = TRUE), 
    n = n()) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(avg_sleep, avg_usage), 
    names_to = "measure", 
    values_to = "average") 

ggplot(useage_summary, aes(MH_cate, average, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#4A78A6", "#6AA6A6")) +
  labs(x = "Mental Health Category", y = "Average (Hours)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| title: Most Used Platform by Academic Level

social <- social |>
  mutate(

social |>
```

### Column {width= "50%"}

```{r}

assign_region <- function(country_vec) {
 
  df <- tibble(Country = country_vec) |>
    mutate(
      Region = countrycode(Country, 
                           origin = "country.name", destination = "region"),
      Continent = countrycode(Country, 
                              origin = "country.name", destination = "continent")
    )
  
  # Warn about unmatched countries
  unmatched <- df$Country[is.na(df$Region)]
  if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
    warning("Unmatched countries: ",
            paste(unique(unmatched), 
                  collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  return(df)
}

region_df <- assign_region(social$Country)

social <- social |>
  left_join(region_df, 
            by = "Country", 
            relationship = "many-to-many")
```

```{r}
)
```

## Row

### Column {width = "60%"}

```{r}
# Countries
#| title: Hours Slept vs Hours Spent on Social Media by Country 



 
# Highlights the countries 
country_highlight <- c(
  "Germany", "Australia", "USA", "UK", "Sri Lanka", "Russia", 
   "Maldives", "Pakistan", "Iraq", "Ghana", "Finland", "Panama", "China", 
  "Mexico", "Trinidad",  "Argentina", "Japan"
)

# Creates a new dataframe summarizing aspects in the regions 
region_summary <- social |>
  group_by(Region, Country) |>
  summarize(
    avg_sleep = mean(Sleep_Hours_Per_Night, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_daily_use = mean(Avg_Daily_Usage_Hours, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

region_summary <- region_summary |>
  mutate(
    label = ifelse(Country %in% country_highlight, Country, "")
  )

# Colors
Region_cols <- c(
  "#4A78A6",
  "#6AA6A6",
  "#C27A7A",
  "#555555",
  "#8FA9C9",  
  "#C9A27A",  
  "#3F6F6F"
)

# Plotting the region summary
ggplot(region_summary, aes(avg_daily_use, avg_sleep)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = Region, fill = Region),
    size = 2.5, alpha = 0.5,
    shape = 21
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = label),
    color = "black",
    size = 9/.pt,
    point.padding = 0.1, 
    box.padding = 0.6,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    max.overlaps = 1000,
    seed = 7654
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = darken(Region_cols, 0.3)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = Region_cols) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Average Nightly Hours Slept",
    limits = c(4.5, 8.5),        # ← ZOOMED IN
    breaks = seq(4.5, 8.5, 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Daily Average of Hours Spent on Social Media",
    limits = c(2, 6.5),          # ← ZOOMED IN
    breaks = seq(2, 6.5, 0.5),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      nrow = 2,
      override.aes = list(
        shape = rep(21, length(unique(region_summary$Region)))
      )
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal_hgrid(12, rel_small = 1) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "right",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(0, "pt")
  )
```

# About The Data

::: {}
  This dataset contains **705 student responses**. Here we have general graphs summarizing a majority of the data. We found that more sleep and less hours slept led to a higher mental health score. This means that those who are happier sleep more and spend less time on their phones. We have the most observations for the 19 year old age group. We have over 100 countries and 7 total regions. A majority of our data is coming from Asia and Europe. It appears that Mexico has the least amount of average sleep and the highest average screen time, while Germany is the opposite. There does appear to be a relationship between average hours of screen time and the amount of sleep people get. Region may slightly effect this. Students prefer TikTok and Instagram as their most used platforms. As academic level increases, so does the effect of social media on academic performance. Instagram is the most used social media for all grade levels, but high school does not use facebook at all. The average mental health of male students is slightly higher than that of female students according to the graph. However, both genders have an average mental health score above 6 and below 7 indicating that the difference in average mental health scores between genders may not be significant. The range is roughly similar across each gender per each amount of conflict over social media with the exception of zero conflicts. Within zero conflicts, there is only data reflecting male students (which the range is roughly zero to three hours with a mean of roughly 1.75 hours). This indicates, that female students engage in at least one conflict per daily use. Furthermore, with the exception of zero conflicts, the mean is roughly the same across genders per conflict increments. There is no clear pattern of lesser or more daily usage hours within gender per conflicts. Lastly, due to the range and mean being so similar across genders, we can see that there is a clear pattern between the average daily usage hours and conflicts over social media. The longer the daily usage is, the more conflicts over social media. 
:::
